category_title: Active and physically competent children with speech and developmental delays
minimal_context: Jamie is outdoors playing with hoops and attempting to roll them along the playground with peer volunteers.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's play with these hoops outdoors. Try rolling your hoop along the playground.

STUDENT: (Holds a hoop and watches with interest as the others roll hoops along the playground.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and try throwing it.

STUDENT: (Throws the hoop. It does not get far before falling to the ground, but he jumps up and down in excitement, picks it up and has another more successful attempt.)

TUTOR: Let me help you with that. (Steps in to help him hold the hoop and roll it in a hand-over-hand way)

STUDENT: (His spontaneity and independent goal-oriented play are gone. He stops jumping and loses his excitement while being physically directed.)

options.A: Permanently and thoroughly keep an eye on the student's physical safety, setting the hoops back into place as soon as they are moved.
options.B: Bend down to eye level and use direct verbal instruction to enforce safety rules ('You're not actually hitting people with the hoop, are you?').
options.C: Participate in the student's game as a peer (leaping over the hoop in motion) and provide social reinforcement (clapping).
options.D: Leave the student free to choose any format and materials they like to use while playing with the hoops.
